description: The pie chart represents the distribution of various news sources, comparing their relative proportions. The chart is divided into 16 slices, each labeled with a distinct news source. The slices are colored differently, although some colors are similar, making it challenging to distinguish between them. The proportions of the slices are labeled with percentage values, ranging from 3% to 14%. The largest slice, "Breitbart," is dark blue and accounts for approximately 14%, followed by "Other" in dark gray at 13%, and "PoliticusUSA" and "Shareblue" combined in light purple at 3% each, with "Fox News" and "CNN" also at 3% each in yellow and red, respectively. The remaining slices are labeled as "Daily Kos" (3%, light green), "National Review" (3%, brown), "Daily Beast" (3%, teal), "RT" (3%, gray), "BBC" (4%, dark gray), "The Guardian" (5%, purple), "Vox" (6%, pink), "NPR" (7%, maroon), "The Huffington Post" (8%, red), "The Daily Caller" (8%, green), and "Drudge Report" (8%, orange). The chart does not include a legend, and the percentage labels are placed inside the slices. The slices appear to be ordered in a clockwise direction by size, with the largest slice starting at the top right.
